messages:
Alex R: Quick heads-up — I saw a ~12% p99 latency regression on the 1e6 token end-to-end benchmark after the qkv-pack change landed on main. Profiling points at epilogue write stalls when qkv-packing is on and paged-KV is active. Putting initial logs here.
Mira L: ugh. which config/bench? small batches or big ones? seq len? any difference when quantized?
Alex R: bench command: `./bench_runner --model redwood-7b --variant fused-attn --batch 32 --seq 1024 --kv-mode paged --qkv-pack true --reps 2000`
Alex R: perf snippet:
```
[perf-summary]
fused_attn_qkvpack kernel: 18.3 ms  (+12.1%)
epilogue_write: 4.9 ms  (+79.4%)
L2_miss_rate: 12.3% -> 28.7%
KV_prefetch_hit_ratio: 0.92 -> 0.67
smem_bank_conflicts: +4.2%
```
Sam T: interesting — the epilogue write jump + L2 miss increase suggests packing changes shifted write pattern so it no longer streams nicely into L2/L1. Could be stride change or different lane layout.
Jonah P: did you try smaller batch? maybe batching heuristics hide it. Also check lane->thread mapping; pack might change coalescing.
Alex R: ran quick compare: batch 8 vs 32
- batch 8: p99 delta +2%
- batch 32: p99 delta +12%
So worse at larger batches.
Mira L: that screams contention at shared caches or higher pressure on epilogue's writeback phase. Paged KV means our prefetcher touches pages while epilogue writes back; if packing makes outputs larger per-thread, writeback can evict prefetched KV lines.
Sam T: can you dump occupancy/active warps and gld/gst counters? also dump access stride histogram for epilogue writes.
Alex R: attached counter dump (trimmed): `gld_inst 1.2e6 gst_inst 8.4e5 l2_lookup 3.1e5 l2_miss 9.2e4 st_instr 5.5e5 bank_conflicts 2300`
Jonah P: another hypothesis: qkv-pack fused the bias/rope earlier so epilogue now interleaves bias add + rope which increases non-contiguous writes vs prior contiguous write of output buffer. Non-contiguous writes -> worse caching.
Mira L: if that's the case, a simple mitigation is to reorder epilogue so we finish writes for a tile before doing page touch/prefetch for KV. Could add a micro-batch barrier or prefetch schedule tweak.
Sam T: or try a soft heuristic: when paged KV is enabled and batch>=16, disable qkv-pack epilogue fusion path and fallback to the previous epilogue ordering. We already have a kernel chooser; add a runtime rule: if (kv_mode==paged && batch>=16 && seq>=512) prefer non-packed-epilogue.
Alex R: I prototyped runtime toggle. With fallback the p99 delta goes to +1.5% (essentially neutral) but throughput drops 3% overall. Tradeoff might be acceptable for stability.
perf-bot: automated alert created: PERF-2981 — fused_attn_qkvpack: p99 regression detected on main. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/alerts/2981
Jonah P: can we do a narrower fix? maybe change epilogue store coalescing: use temporary per-thread contiguous buffer and memcpy out to final location to restore streaming behavior. That may add a small copy but improve L2 behavior.
Mira L: also try changing prefetch distance for paged-KV when packing is on; if prefetch is too late, epilogue writebacks race with page fills.
Alex R: plan:
- short: add runtime chooser to fallback (merged to canary, rolling out to 20% capacity)
- investigate: add stride histogram + per-kernel store pattern tracer
- experiment: transient thread-local buffer + memcpy vs reorder epilogue ops
- experiment: adjust KV prefetch distance under qkv-pack
Sam T: I'll add a micro-benchmark to isolate just epilogue store patterns and run on curated seq dist (many short + many long). Put results in the perf dashboard.
Jonah P: cc @eng-runtime for visibility. we should also add a regression test that runs packed qkv + paged-KV at batch 32 in CI perf daily.
Alex R: yep opened PRs/links: https://github.com/redwoodinc/infra/pull/783 (runtime chooser) and https://github.com/redwoodinc/benchmarks/issues/421 (epilogue store tracer)
Mira L: thanks — good triage. If anyone finds a quick kernel patch with negligible perf cost, ping and we'll flip canary to 100%.
Sam T: reassigning to me for epilogue tracer work. will post updates later today.
Alex R: thanks all :thumbsup:
